subproblem.title: Coinvariance of the given subalgebra
subproblem.statement: Let k be a field, H a commutative Hopf k-algebra, and K a k-subalgebra such that Δ_H(K) lies in the k-linear span of tensors with both factors in K. Let B be a commutative k-bialgebra and q:H→B a bialgebra homomorphism. If ker(q) is the ideal generated by {t∈K:ε_H(t)=0}, then K≤HopfAlgebra.hopfKer q, where Hopf-kernel membership means (id_H⊗q)Δ_H(x)=x⊗1_B.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {k : Type*} [Field k] {H : Type*} [CommRing H] [HopfAlgebra k H] (K : Subalgebra k H) (hΔ : (∀ x ∈ K, Coalgebra.comul (R := k) x ∈ Submodule.span k {t : TensorProduct k H H | ∃ a ∈ K, ∃ b ∈ K, t = TensorProduct.tmul k a b})) {B : Type*} [CommRing B] [Bialgebra k B] (q : BialgHom k H B) (hker : (RingHom.ker (q : H →+* B) = Ideal.span {x : H | x ∈ K ∧ Coalgebra.counit (R := k) x = 0})), K ≤ HopfAlgebra.hopfKer q
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Write ε for the counit of H. For t∈K put u=t−algebraMap(k,H)(ε(t)). The subalgebra contains scalar images and is closed under subtraction, so u∈K. Since ε is a k-algebra homomorphism, ε(u)=ε(t)−ε(t)=0.
2. Thus u belongs to the generating set of the ideal in hker, hence to ker(q). Preservation of scalar images by q gives q(t)=algebraMap(k,B)(ε(t)) for every t∈K.
3. For x∈K, hΔ expresses Δ_H(x) as a finite k-linear combination of pure tensors with both factors in K. Absorbing each scalar coefficient into its first factor gives Δ_H(x)=Σ_i a_i⊗b_i with a_i,b_i∈K.
4. Apply id_H⊗q and use step 2. The result is Σ_i a_i⊗algebraMap(k,B)(ε(b_i))=(Σ_i ε(b_i)a_i)⊗1_B. The right counit identity applied to the expression in step 3 gives Σ_i ε(b_i)a_i=x. Therefore (id_H⊗q)Δ_H(x)=x⊗1_B.
5. This is exactly the defining membership equation of HopfAlgebra.hopfKer q. It holds for every x∈K, proving K≤HopfAlgebra.hopfKer q.
proof_key_steps: Subtract the counit scalar to obtain an augmentation generator in K.
Use the kernel equality to determine q on K.
Expand comultiplication with both tensor factors in K.
Use the right counit identity to obtain coinvariance.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type agree, including the precise augmentation-ideal kernel equality. Subtracting the counit scalar determines q on K; coproduct stability and right counitality then give the defining Hopf-kernel equation. The proof needs neither surjectivity nor antipode stability and has no undeclared dependency.
